    HIGH missing-hsts via header-analysis

    Missing HSTS header

    💡 Add strict-transport-security header to improve security

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — missing-hsts
    What it means

    The site’s HTTP responses lack the Strict‑Transport‑Security (HSTS) header, which tells browsers to only use HTTPS.

    Why it matters

    Without HSTS, users can be exposed to downgrade attacks or man‑in‑the‑middle attacks that force them onto an insecure connection, compromising data integrity and trust.

    Recommended fix

    Configure the web server to send a Strict‑Transport‑Security header, such as "Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload", to enforce HTTPS for all future requests.

    HIGH missing-csp via header-analysis

    Missing CSP header

    💡 Add content-security-policy header to improve security

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — missing-csp
    What it means

    The site does not send a Content‑Security‑Policy (CSP) header, so browsers have no instructions on which resources are allowed to load or execute.

    Why it matters

    Without CSP, attackers can inject malicious scripts, steal data, or hijack the page, increasing the risk of cross‑site scripting (XSS) and data exfiltration. It also reduces the ability to mitigate other injection attacks.

    Recommended fix

    Add a CSP header that specifies trusted sources for scripts, styles, images, and other resources. Start with a restrictive policy such as "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self';" and adjust as needed for third‑party content.

    MEDIUM missing-x-content-type-options via header-analysis

    Missing X-Content-Type-Options header

    💡 Add x-content-type-options header to improve security

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — missing-x-content-type-options
    What it means

    The site is missing the X‑Content‑Type‑Options header, so browsers may attempt to sniff the MIME type of responses.

    Why it matters

    MIME sniffing can allow an attacker to treat a non‑script file as executable, leading to XSS or other content‑type confusion attacks. It also weakens the site’s defense against certain types of content‑type attacks.

    Recommended fix

    Add the header "X‑Content‑Type‑Options: nosniff" to all responses. This tells browsers to honor the declared Content‑Type and not guess.

    MEDIUM missing-x-frame-options via header-analysis

    Missing X-Frame-Options header

    💡 Add x-frame-options header to improve security

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — missing-x-frame-options
    What it means

    The site does not send an X‑Frame‑Options header, so its pages can be embedded in iframes on other sites.

    Why it matters

    Allowing framing exposes the site to clickjacking attacks, where a malicious site overlays the page and tricks users into interacting with hidden elements. It also can lead to UI redress and phishing risks.

    Recommended fix

    Add the header "X‑Frame‑Options: SAMEORIGIN" (or "DENY" if the site should never be framed). This prevents other sites from embedding the page in a frame.

    MEDIUM sensitive-url via crawl-analysis

    URL may contain sensitive data: https://cityhangaround.com/forgot-password

    https://cityhangaround.com/forgot-password

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — sensitive-url
    What it means

    The URL path for the forgot‑password page may expose sensitive information, such as user identifiers or tokens, in the browser address bar or server logs.

    Why it matters

    Sensitive data in URLs can be inadvertently shared through referrer headers, browser history, or server logs, increasing the risk of credential leakage or phishing attacks.

    Recommended fix

    Move any sensitive parameters to the request body or use secure, short‑lived tokens passed via POST. Ensure the page is served over HTTPS and consider adding HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS).

    MEDIUM sensitive-url via crawl-analysis

    URL may contain sensitive data: https://cityhangaround.com/auth/google

    https://cityhangaround.com/auth/google

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — sensitive-url
    What it means

    The Google authentication endpoint’s URL may contain sensitive data, such as authorization codes or tokens, in the query string.

    Why it matters

    Exposing tokens in URLs can lead to credential theft via logs, browser history, or accidental sharing, compromising user accounts and site security.

    Recommended fix

    Use POST requests or redirect mechanisms that place tokens in the request body or secure cookies. Enforce HTTPS and implement HSTS to protect the data in transit.

    MEDIUM sensitive-url via crawl-analysis

    URL may contain sensitive data: https://cityhangaround.com/auth/facebook

    https://cityhangaround.com/auth/facebook

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — sensitive-url
    What it means

    The Facebook authentication endpoint’s URL may include sensitive information, like access tokens or user identifiers, in the query string.

    Why it matters

    Sensitive data in URLs can be captured in logs, referrer headers, or browser history, creating a vector for attackers to hijack sessions or impersonate users.

    Recommended fix

    Transition to POST requests or use secure, short‑lived tokens that are not exposed in the URL. Ensure all authentication flows occur over HTTPS and enable HSTS to mitigate interception risks.

    MEDIUM multiple-h1

    Multiple H1 tags found (4)

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — multiple-h1
    What it means

    The page contains four H1 tags instead of a single top‑level heading.

    Why it matters

    Search engines expect one H1 to understand the main topic of a page. Multiple H1s can dilute keyword signals, confuse crawlers, and may negatively impact rankings or accessibility for screen readers.

    Recommended fix

    Replace the extra H1 tags with H2 or H3 headings, keeping only one H1 that accurately describes the page’s primary content. Ensure the remaining headings follow a logical hierarchy.

    MEDIUM missing-canonical

    No canonical URL specified

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — missing-canonical
    What it means

    The page does not include a canonical link element to declare its preferred URL.

    Why it matters

    Without a canonical tag, search engines may index duplicate or similar URLs, splitting ranking signals and potentially causing content to be considered duplicate. This can reduce visibility and dilute SEO value.

    Recommended fix

    Add a canonical tag in the page’s head, e.g., <link rel="canonical" href="https://cityhangaround.com/">, to indicate the authoritative URL for the content.

    ✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — broken-link
    What it means

    The audit found that the link to https://cityhangaround.com/pages could not be reached because the request timed out. This indicates that the page is currently unavailable or the server is not responding to the request.

    Why it matters

    A broken link prevents users from accessing content, leading to frustration and a negative user experience. It can also negatively impact search engine rankings and reduce trust in the site.

    Recommended fix

    Verify that the page exists and is correctly deployed on the server. Check server logs for timeout errors, increase timeout settings if necessary, and update or remove the link once the page is restored.
